explanation: Gene mutations are classified as either spontaneous or induced. Spontaneous mutations happen without external influence, arising from chemical changes in DNA that cause mispairing during replication, the movement of mobile genetic elements called transposons from one chromosomal location to another, or general replication errors. During replication, DNA polymerase proofreads new strands and typically corrects errors; because of this, the overall spontaneous mutation rate is low, at 1 in 1,000,000,000 (1 billion) nucleotide pairs replicated. In contrast, induced mutations are caused by environmental mutagens, such as radiation (e.g., Ultraviolet Radiation) and organic chemicals (e.g., Tobacco Smoke). Many mutagens are carcinogens, meaning they are cancer-causing substances.
